book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: One helps to get players to move the ball

parts.note: a side is a team of players
what a footballer does to send the ball on

explanation.surface: A football helper whose job is getting the team to pass the ball about.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is an assistant or companion who supports the main figure, a junior partner.

clue.text: Second superior intake

parts.note: the abbreviation for second
upper means higher in rank

explanation.surface: A further, higher-ranking group of new recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: Intake suggests new pupils or recruits; here it means food taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, an occasion of eating food, which is a kind of intake.

clue.text: Move to plunge right inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: to dive is to plunge
the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A swimmer told to get in and plunge straight down.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to propel or push forward, making something go along, so it means move.

clue.text: Flier on line

parts.note: surface reading: an aviator or a leaflet, perhaps travelling or posted online
setter's reading: a toy that flies tethered at the end of a string

explanation.walkthrough: On line hints at the internet; it is the string held by someone on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a light frame covered in fabric that is flown in the wind while held by a long string.

clue.text: Trick to watch out for when depressed

parts.note: a con is a swindle
cave is Latin for beware, old schoolboy slang for look out

explanation.surface: A warning to look out for swindlers when one is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Cave (pronounced KAY-vee) was the public-school lookout's cry of warning, from Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A concave surface curves inward, hollowed or sunk like a dent, so it is pressed in.

clue.text: One takes steps the German can somehow take in

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unstated new arrangement
to take in is to hold inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stepping out while a German grudgingly copes with something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer is a person whose art is moving the feet in rhythmic patterns to music.

clue.text: Risk finding no dead heat

indicators.note: finding none of something means it is left out

parts.note: danger is risk
the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A race finish declared not to be a dead heat, a matter of risk.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead heat is a tied race, but the words split: dead is a letter to drop, heat the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat can mean passion or fury, as in the heat of an argument, so it is a synonym of rage.

clue.text: Roman officer in counter manoeuvre

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman officer engaged in a counterattack.
explanation.definitionFit: A centurion commanded a company of about a hundred legionaries in the ancient Roman army.

clue.text: Something to pay to accommodate players living here

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: rent is a regular payment
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A landlord charging rent to house a team who live on the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone who lives in a particular place, as opposed to a visitor or guest.

clue.text: The art of putting on a coat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fine art of making pictures in pigment
second meaning: applying a layer, as a decorator does to a wall

explanation.walkthrough: A coat here is a layer of paint, not a garment; the clue reads like a lesson in dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the artistic craft of pictures in oils and the decorator's job of applying layers to walls.

clue.text: They may represent a convenience

parts.note: taken as written
a public convenience is a lavatory; the men's one is the gents

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that some facility stands for something.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public convenience is a public toilet, and the gents is the men's.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of clients, so they are people who may speak for or stand in for others.

clue.text: Not the talk you usually hear in Battersea Park

definitions.text: Not the talk you usually hear in Battersea Park

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the next word

parts.note: the middle letters of the place name

explanation.surface: Remarking that some language is not what one hears in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Park is in south London, where Irish Gaelic is hardly the usual speech; the whole clue defines while the park's name holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Irish or Scottish Gaelic, a language not commonly spoken in London.

clue.text: Flat happening to have no central heating

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from what comes before

parts.note: an event is something that happens, an occurrence

indicators.note: central points to the single letter at the middle of the following word

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters sits in the exact middle

explanation.surface: A rented flat where something has happened to leave it without central heating.
explanation.walkthrough: Central heating looks like the familiar household system, but only the middle letter of heating is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and flat both describe a level surface with no bumps or slopes, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Honest reason for finding somewhere to have fun

parts.note: fair dealing is honest dealing
grounds for something are its reasons

explanation.surface: A sincere justification for seeking out some place of amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an open site holding rides, stalls and amusements for a day out.

clue.text: Mark to round off award

indicators.note: a thing that comes off is detached and removed, so that letter goes from the word

parts.note: the Academy Award statuette
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A grade given to round off a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Round off sounds like finishing something; it says the round letter is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting blemish left on skin by a healed wound, so it is a type of mark.

clue.text: One might get carried away as provider of literature

definitions.text: One might get carried away as provider of literature

parts.note: surface reading: someone overexcited, losing self-control while supplying books

parts.words: carried away as provider of literature
parts.note: setter's reading: a small book format designed to be literally carried about in one's clothing

explanation.walkthrough: Carried away usually means overexcited; here it means physically carried off in a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket edition is a small-format printing of a book, sized so a reader can take it anywhere.

clue.text: Quietly getting to the point of exhortation

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for soft
arriving at, getting to

explanation.surface: Someone talking softly and coming to the heart of an urgent appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Preaching is earnestly urging people toward moral conduct, as in a sermon, which is exhortation.

clue.text: On foot to the Orient

definitions.note: a description of where the answer is, standing in for the noun

parts.note: taken as written
the Orient is the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Walking all the way to the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: On foot looks like walking; it means a part found on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Each foot has five digits at its front end, so this body part is one found on a foot.

clue.text: Not all of Paddy's people show the flag

indicators.note: not all of says the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: Paddy is a nickname for an Irishman

explanation.surface: Some Irish folk waving their national flag.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a national banner; it is the plant, yellow flag being a wild iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the iris plant, especially the yellow flag growing by water.

clue.text: Got together to search one rejected study

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
the Roman numeral

indicators.note: rejected suggests sent back, so the word for study is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study

explanation.surface: People teamed up to search for one turned-down piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined means joined or united, which is what things that have come together have done.

clue.text: Fighting to get out for a change?

definitions.text: Fighting to get out for a change?

parts.note: surface reading: struggling to escape from somewhere, wanting a break
setter's reading: an uprising in plain view whose aim is to overthrow and alter the regime

explanation.walkthrough: For a change sounds like wanting variety; here it means seeking political change, and getting out means coming into the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcealed armed revolt against authority is what the phrase describes, a public uprising rather than a secret plot.

clue.text: Tramp with little money has to make a connection

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant
p is a penny

explanation.surface: A penniless vagrant needing to catch a train.
explanation.walkthrough: Make a connection sounds like catching a train; it means making contact, as when knocking into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump is to knock against or collide with something, so it makes physical contact.

clue.text: Threatening to get weaving?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: appearing ominously, about to happen
second meaning, playfully coined: working a weaver's frame

explanation.walkthrough: Get weaving is British slang for hurry up; here it means literally weaving, with the question mark flagging the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing looms over us, and a loom is the frame for making cloth, giving a whimsical verb.

clue.text: Record turn-up with philosopher in the team

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means flipped to read bottom to top

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
A. J. Ayer, the British philosopher

explanation.surface: A surprising result recorded for a thinker who made the side.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn-up (for the books) is British slang for a surprise, but here it flips the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a member of a team, someone who takes part in the game.

clue.text: Support nonsense game

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
gammon is old slang for humbug or nonsense

explanation.surface: Backing some daft pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Gammon (as in gammon and spinach) is dated British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two players moving counters by throws of dice.

clue.text: Big at holding fire, one hears

indicators.note: one hears says the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a grate is the iron frame in a fireplace that holds the burning coals

explanation.surface: A large gun holding its fire, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Great and big are synonyms, both meaning of large size or extent.

clue.text: Build-up backed as a rule, one learns

indicators.note: backed suggests going backwards, so the word for rule is read from its end

parts.note: a law is a rule
L is the learner, as on the L-plates of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A buildup of pressure handled as a lesson in routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid's checked letters allow several words; law backed plus the learner's L builds WALL, which is something built up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall is a structure raised up course by course from bricks or stone, a thing built up.

clue.text: Be prepared for arrival of a bandsman

parts.note: taken as written
the waits were town musicians who played in the streets, especially at Christmas

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a musician to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: A wait was a member of a band of street musicians or carol singers, an old British term.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to expect it and stand ready for it to come.

clue.text: Incline to reject last letter from a composer

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it out

parts.note: Franz Liszt, Hungarian composer
the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Tending to refuse the final note from a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Last letter looks like the end of the composer's name, but it means the alphabet's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To list is to lean or tilt to one side, as a ship does, which is to incline.

clue.text: Given a fix in deal that's not right

indicators.note: something not right is wrong or amiss, so the letters must be put another way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was rigged in a crooked transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed means fastened or fixed in place, as boards are by driving pins through them.

clue.text: Armed one with brief writing when a girl comes round

indicators.note: coming round something means surrounding it on both sides

parts.note: a common girl's name
the Roman numeral
short for literature

explanation.surface: An armed man with a short note, visited by a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Military means relating to soldiers and armed forces, so the two are close adjectives.

clue.text: Figures they may be on hand

definitions.meaning: second meaning: fingers, which grow from the palm

explanation.walkthrough: On hand normally means available; here it means literally attached to a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both single numerals and fingers or toes, which are body parts used for counting.

clue.text: One causes a stir thanks to being in a European capital on the way back

indicators.note: being in something puts these words inside the other piece
travelling back means the capital's name is spelt from its last letter

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia
ta is informal British for thanks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stirring up trouble while travelling home from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs people up, a troublemaker who incites unrest; the definition plays on stirring liquid.
